properties.name: FIELD REPORT (Alex, workplace project brain, relayed 2026-09-21): ingesting existing repositories cost about $70 of tokens in one day, the export is past 50,000 lines at roughly a quarter done, and duplicate components are still being written
properties.statement: THE FIRST COST MEASUREMENT THIS PROJECT HAS FOR INGEST, and it arrives from a workplace billed per token rather than on a subscription, which is why it was noticed at all. Alex is using reflow2 as a project brain at work, ingesting the contents of several existing project repositories. Reported through Anthony, 2026-09-21: roughly $70 of tokens in one day; the design export is past 50,000 lines; he estimates he is about a quarter of the way through the material. Duplicate components are still being created, and his words for the cause are that reflow2 "had no way to efficiently query what was already in the graph". Each component gets a unique TEXT NAME, and he is reaching for the repository PATH as a unique identifier instead. He also named a second cost that is not tokens: the effort of going through all the code and documentation himself. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE NUMBER. dec:idea-mechanical-code-structure-ingest has been open since 2026-08-06 and argues for extracting the structural half mechanically and spending the model only on intent. Its recorded arguments are about determinism, parser maintenance and the functional-decomposition objection. COST IS NOT AMONG THEM. This is the first evidence that the expensive half is expensive in money, on a real corpus, to a real user, and it is the argument that idea was missing. It also lands on cap:bl-97, which already states that the missing half of folder-scale ingest is identity resolution ACROSS documents — the duplicate-component symptom is that statement arriving from the field. BOUNDS, AND THEY ARE WIDE. Second-hand through one relay. The $70 is his figure and nobody here has seen the billing. No breakdown exists: reading source and documents into context to understand them is irreducible, re-reading the graph to check for duplicates is not, and NOBODY HAS MEASURED WHICH IS WHICH. Those two have opposite fixes, so the number justifies an investigation and does not by itself justify a build. The 50,000 lines and the one-quarter estimate are his too, and a line count of an export is a weak proxy for design size. Anthony flagged the path detail as not making complete sense to him, so it is recorded as reported rather than as understood. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a breakdown of where the tokens go on one representative repository — document reading, graph reading, node writing, retries after a near-match refusal — which only he can take, and which is worth asking for before anything is built.
